headline.statement: Table 3's muscle p-values 0.4146 and 0.4936, and its Combined Wei-Lachin line (MW=0.5611, 95% CI 0.5456-0.5766, N1/N2=10/3, p<0.0001), are digit-for-digit Table 2's histology numbers, not results of the muscle tests printed beside them.
headline.evidence: Table 3 Muscle Marlene p=0.4146 (N1/N2=16/5, MW=0.6250) and Muscle Catoi p=0.4936 (N1/N2=11/2, MW=0.8182, 95% CI 0.5578 to 1.0000); Table 2 NNTXDIAM p=0.4146 and NNTXAREA p=0.4936; both Combined rows MW=0.5611, 95% CI 0.5456-0.5766, N1/N2=10/3, p<0.0001.
headline.plain: The muscle table reuses the nerve-histology table's p-values and its combined 'significant' line, including a sample size that belongs to a different analysis. One pasted p-value says 'not significant' while that row's own interval already rules out no difference.

findings.title: Table 3 muscle p-values and Combined row are Table 2's histology numbers
findings.reported: Table 3 Muscle Marlene: MW=0.6250, 95% CI 0.3993 to 0.8507, N1/N2=16/5, p=0.4146. Muscle Catoi: MW=0.8182, 95% CI 0.5578 to 1.0000, N1/N2=11/2, p=0.4936. Combined (Wei-Lachin): MW=0.5611, 95% CI 0.5456 to 0.5766, N1/N2=10/3, p<0.0001. Table 2 NNTXDIAM p=0.4146 and NNTXAREA p=0.4936; Table 2 Combined is the same MW, CI, N1/N2 and p as Table 3 Combined.
findings.computed: detect_duplication: two identical (0.4146, 0.4936) and (0.5611, 0.5456) pairs across Table 2 and Table 3 (coincidence probability about 1.6e-13). grimu_check: p=0.4146 matches no U for 16 versus 5 (nearest U=29.5 p=0.409, U=30 p=0.4328); p=0.4936 matches no U for 11 versus 2 (nearest U=7 p=0.4897 and 0.5128). check_estimate_ci on Muscle Catoi: CI excludes the Mann-Whitney null of 0.5 while p=0.4936 is not significant (recovered Wald p=0.0048; lower bound 0.5578 does not depend on the truncated upper bound of 1.0000). Table 3 Combined MW=0.5611 with N1/N2=10/3 lies below both printed muscle MWs (0.6250 and 0.8182) and does not use 16/5 or 11/2.
findings.assumptions: Table 2 (nerve histometrics) and Table 3 (muscle fibre diameter) are different outcome families, so identical p-values, Combined MW/CI and N1/N2 are not a legitimate reuse of one analysis. Muscle fibre diameter is a continuous micrometre measure, so the GRIM-U lattice is the untied one. Mann-Whitney null is 0.5 as implied by the paper's MW definition P(X<Y)+0.5P(X=Y). The modal innocent cause is a forest-plot template copied from Table 2 into Table 3 without recomputing.
findings.plain: The muscle results table reuses the nerve-histology table's p-values and its combined 'significant' line, right down to a 10-versus-3 sample size that is not the muscle rows' 16-versus-5 or 11-versus-2. For one muscle comparison the printed interval already excludes no difference, so that comparison would be significant, but the pasted p-value says it is not. The likely slip is a copied figure template; as printed, Table 3 does not report the muscle tests it names.

consequence.explanation: Table 3's Combined p<0.0001 is Table 2's histology combination, not a combination of the muscle rows; Muscle Catoi's own interval excludes 0.5 while the pasted p=0.4936 is non-significant.

findings.reproduction_problem: THE COMMAND DISAGREES WITH THE FINDING: it reports `suspicious` where the finding claims `highly_suspicious`. The command ran perfectly well -- that is the point. Re-read the finding before the paper.

findings.title: NNTXMAX interval excludes no difference while p=0.9017 does not
findings.reported: NNTXMAX MW=0.8000, 95% CI 0.5362 to 1.0000, N1/N2=10/3, p=0.9017. Methods: alpha=0.05 and two-sided 95% CIs.
findings.computed: check_estimate_ci: CI excludes the null of 0.5 while reported p=0.9017 is not significant; recovered Wald p=0.0112 (upper bound truncated at 1.0000, so that recovered p is not a trustworthy point estimate). The printed lower bound 0.5362>0.5 does not depend on that truncation. grimu_check: p=0.9017 matches no U for 10 versus 3 (nearest U=13.5 p=0.8658, U=14 p=0.9326), which is the p of a near-null rank sum, not of MW=0.8000.
findings.assumptions: The paper's MW null is 0.5. A two-sided 95% CI that does not contain 0.5 and a two-sided p>0.05 cannot both be from the same test of that null. Wald inversion of a CI truncated at 1.0 is not used as the primary evidence; the printed lower bound is. Interval construction is not named beyond 'two-sided 95% CI' of the Mann-Whitney statistic, so an exact or bootstrap interval remains an open innocent reading for the recovered Wald p, not for the lower bound versus 0.5.
findings.plain: For one nerve-fibre measure the authors print an interval that already rules out no difference, which at their stated 5% threshold would be a significant result, and a p-value of 0.9017 that says the opposite. Those two numbers cannot both describe the same test.

passages.quote: The level of alpha was defined as alpha=0.05, and a two-sided test was used for superiority.
passages.label: Statistical Methods

consequence.explanation: This component would be significant at the paper's alpha=0.05 if the printed 95% CI is believed, but the printed p=0.9017 is not.

findings.title: None of Table 2's eight component p-values is a Mann-Whitney p for 10 versus 3 animals
findings.reported: Eight component rows at N1/N2=10/3 with p=0.4146, 0.4936, 0.1928, 0.1020, 0.7533, 0.9017, 0.2347, 0.3505, attributed to the Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney / Wei-Lachin family. NNTXDIAM and NNTXAREA share MW=0.4000 and 95% CI 0.0704 to 0.7296 but not the same p. NNTXTOTAL MW=0.5667, 95% CI 0.2855 to 0.8479, p=0.2347.
findings.computed: grimu_coexistence: 8 of 8 p-values individually flagged; none matches an achievable U under exact, normal, or continuity-corrected conventions; no pairwise co-existence violation; floor p exact=0.00699; 45 achievable p-values at 4 dp. One-sided re-run of p=0.4146 also unmatched. check_estimate_ci on NNTXTOTAL (interval symmetric about the printed MW, so not truncated): recovered p=0.642 versus printed 0.2347. Shared NNTXDIAM/NNTXAREA CI recovers Wald p=0.552, which matches neither printed p.
findings.assumptions: The paper attributes these p-values to Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney tests at the printed 10/3. Diameter, area, myelin and related histometrics are continuous, so the default is no ties; a tie-corrected lattice was not used. Rule 12 caps a granularity miss at suspicious. Rank-sum packages can shift a p in the fourth decimal; they do not print eight unachievable values. Different tie corrections could split two p-values but would not be expected to leave MW and the 95% CI identical to four decimals.
findings.reproduction: metascience grimu-coexist --n1 10 --n2 3 --p-values 0.4146,0.4936,0.1928,0.1020,0.7533,0.9017,0.2347,0.3505 --decimals 4 --method both --test-type mann_whitney --p-source unspecified --ties-possible false
findings.plain: The eight individual nerve-fibre p-values are presented as rank-sum tests on 10 versus 3 animals, but none of those eight numbers is a p-value that a rank-sum test on 10 versus 3 can produce. Two rows even share the same effect size and the same interval yet print different p-values. These component tests were all called non-significant, so the mismatch does not flip those calls; it means the printed p-column is not the test the methods describe.

passages.quote: The analysis was performed by means of the highly efficient Wei-Lachin procedure, a multivariate generalization of the Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney test.
passages.label: Statistical Methods

consequence.explanation: All eight component tests remain non-significant under the printed p-values; the lattice misses do not flip those NS calls.

findings.title: Day-90 n and CMAP-positive counts do not agree across Abstract, Results, figures and Table 4
findings.location: Abstract; Results, Surgery; Figure 4 caption; Discussion after Figure 12; Table 4; Table 2 N1/N2
findings.reported: Abstract: 2nd Op at day 90 in 16 surviving rats; eight rats showed positive CMAPs. Results: 21 rats underwent the 2nd Op; electro-stimulation of the PNG transplant in 21 rats was positive in only 8 rats. Figure 4: 8 of 16 rats. Discussion after Figure 12: 7 out of the 14 surviving animals. Table 4 lists seven (+) cases and ten (−) cases. Table 2 Combined and components use N1/N2=10/3.
findings.computed: Stage-1 check_summation_batch: randomized 12+11+7=30, completers 5+7+3=15, and the Results early-death addends summing to 9 are internally additive (30−9=21). Abstract 16 is not that cascade. Table 4 7+10=17; tissues from No 21 and No 28 (died at the 2nd Op) are said to have been saved, which can explain 15+2=17 rows but not 8 versus 7 positives. Table 2's 10/3 matches none of 8 vs 8, 8 vs 13, 7 vs 10, or 16 vs 5.
findings.assumptions: Stimulus yes versus no is the grouping for Tables 2 and 3. Completer identities in Results (15 named animals) plus saved 2nd-Op deaths (No 21, 28) are the paper's own accounting. Direct check_summation was denied at this stage; additive identities are taken from Stage-1 check_summation_batch, which found those identities consistent.
findings.plain: The authors never settle how many rats reached the day-90 operation (16 in the abstract, 21 in the Results) or how many had a positive muscle signal (eight in the abstract and Results, eight of 16 on one figure, seven of 14 in the Discussion, seven plus-cases in Table 4). The only significant combined test is run as 10 versus 3, which matches none of those splits. The Results death tally adds up on its own; the abstract's 16 does not.

passages.quote: 2nd Op at day 90 (16 surviving rats) for open proof of reinnervation
passages.label: Abstract

passages.quote: Consequently, 21 rats underwent the 2 nd Op for transplant revision
passages.label: Results, Surgery

consequence.explanation: Stimulus yes versus no is the grouping for the paper's only significant combined test, but the paper never pins down how many animals were yes.

findings.title: Vecuronium dose is 0.04–0.05 mg/kg in Table 1 and 80 µg/kg in Figure 5
findings.location: Table 1, Vecuronium row versus Figure 5 caption
findings.reported: Table 1: Vecuronium 0.04 - 0.05 mg/kg IV. Figure 5: Vecuronium IV (80 µg/kg). Four CMAP-positive rats received it.
findings.computed: check_ratio: 80/1000=0.08, so 80 µg/kg is 0.08 mg/kg, which sits outside Table 1's 0.04-0.05 mg/kg range. Equivalently, Table 1's range is 40-50 µg/kg.
findings.assumptions: 1000 µg=1 mg is a unit identity, not a scale the paper had to state. The two printed doses are different quantities; four CMAP-positive rats are the subset that received the drug.
findings.plain: The drug used to show mixed nerve-to-muscle signalling is given as 0.04 to 0.05 milligrams per kilogram in the dosing table and as 80 micrograms per kilogram on the figure, which is 0.08 milligrams per kilogram. Those are not the same dose.

passages.quote: Vecuronium ® IV (80 µg/kg) application during artificial ventilation of the rat
passages.label: Figure 5 caption

consequence.explanation: Vecuronium response is the functional proof offered for mixed cholinergic/glutamatergic transmission; the dose used is not a single printed number.

findings.title: EMG-positive angiogenesis scores of '2 and 3' versus Table 4 case 6 scored 1
findings.location: Figure 9 caption versus Table 4, case 6 ang cell
findings.reported: Angiogenesis was more intense in EMG-positive cases (individual final scores of 2 and 3; score average 2.57) than in EMG-negative cases (individual final scores of 1 and 2; score average 1.3). Table 4 case 6 (+) lists ang (1); case 28 (+) has no ang grade printed. Methods grade angiogenesis 0-3.
findings.computed: check_ratio: EMG-negative average 1.3 follows from Table 4 grades summing to 13 over 10 cases. grim_check: mean 2.57 is attainable at n=7 on a 0-3 integer scale (18/7=2.57). Stage-1: no combination of the printed positive ang grades (2, 1, 3, 3, 2, 3) averages to 2.57. Case 6 (+) scored 1 contradicts 'individual final scores of 2 and 3'.
findings.assumptions: Table 4 integer ang grades are the 'individual final scores' the caption describes. n=7 for GRIM is the count of (+) cases in Table 4, which the caption does not print beside 2.57. Final scores are means over high-power fields, so 2.57 could in principle be a mean of means rather than an average of integer grades; the caption's 'individual final scores of 2 and 3' is what collides with case 6.
findings.plain: The authors say EMG-positive animals had only angiogenesis scores of 2 and 3, averaging 2.57, but Table 4 gives case 6, which is EMG-positive, a score of 1. The EMG-negative average of 1.3 does match that table. This is a descriptive contrast, not a hypothesis test.

passages.quote: was more intense in EMG-positive cases (individual final scores of 2 and 3; score average 2.57) than in EMG-negative cases (individual final scores of 1 and 2; score average 1.3)
passages.label: Figure 9 caption / Angiogenesis

passages.quote: Gc (1); fibr (3); Sc in SC (1), ang (1); Npres (1).

findings.title: Methods specify a two-sided test; table captions specify a directional test
findings.location: Statistical Methods versus Table 2/3 captions and Statistical Evaluation
findings.reported: Methods: 'The level of alpha was defined as alpha=0.05, and a two-sided test was used for superiority' and 'two-sided 95% confidence intervals'. Table 3 caption and Statistical Evaluation: 'Wei-Lachin procedure, directional test, exploratory interpretation.'
findings.computed: grimu_check one-sided on p=0.4146 at 10 versus 3 still unmatched. Which tail produced the p-column is not recoverable, because those p-values miss both the two-sided and one-sided 10-versus-3 lattices.
findings.assumptions: The paper also labels the analysis exploratory and warns about small n. Both phrases cannot be the procedure that produced the p-column; the printed p-values do not adjudicate which phrase was used.
findings.plain: The methods say tests were two-sided; the table captions say the combined test was directional. The printed p-values do not match either version of a 10-versus-3 rank-sum test, so a reader cannot tell which rule was used.

passages.quote: Wei-Lachin procedure, directional test, exploratory interpretation

report_markdown:
This study randomises 30 rats to Cerebrolysin, saline, or no injection after a T10 sural-nerve graft into the internal oblique, and asks whether the graft reinnervates muscle with mixed cholinergic and glutamatergic transmission. The only statistically significant test the authors report is a Wei-Lachin combination of histometric nerve measures comparing 'stimulus yes' with 'stimulus no' (MW=0.5611, 95% CI 0.5456-0.5766, p<0.0001). They call the analysis exploratory, skip multiplicity adjustment, and warn about small samples.

Twenty of the thirty-four checks that ran on printed values passed. The randomisation split 12+11+7 sums to 30, the completers 5+7+3 sum to 15, 15 deaths among 30 print as 50%, all eleven Mann-Whitney point estimates sit inside their printed intervals, and the Combined estimate, interval and p<0.0001 agree with one another on a Wald reading. That is the part that holds.

What does not hold is the rest of those same tables, and it reaches the result the paper depends on. Table 3 is offered as muscle-fibre evidence of reinnervation. Its first two p-values are Table 2's first two p-values, and its Combined line is Table 2's Combined line, including N1/N2=10/3 rather than the muscle rows' 16/5 and 11/2. Table 3's caption even describes 'the combined result of the two histological assessments' while sitting on a muscle table. The ordinary reading is a forest-plot template reused without recomputing. As printed, Table 3 does not report the muscle tests it names. Muscle Catoi's own interval already excludes no difference (lower bound 0.5578), so that comparison would be significant at the authors' 5% threshold; the pasted p=0.4936 is not. A rank-sum p of 0.4146 is also not a possible value for 16 versus 5 animals, nor is 0.4936 possible for 11 versus 2.

The source table is not internally coherent either. None of the eight Table 2 component p-values is an achievable Mann-Whitney p for 10 versus 3 animals, two-sided or one-sided. Rank-sum software can move a p in the fourth decimal; it does not emit eight unachievable values. Two rows share MW=0.4000 and the same 95% CI to four decimals yet print different p-values. NNTXMAX's interval starts at 0.5362, which already excludes 0.5, while p=0.9017 does not. NNTXTOTAL's interval is symmetric about its MW and recovers p≈0.642 against a printed 0.2347. Methods promise two-sided tests and two-sided 95% CIs of the Mann-Whitney statistic; the captions say 'directional test'. The printed p-values miss both lattices, so the tail convention cannot be recovered from the numbers.

The grouping for the Combined test is never one number. The abstract has 16 rats at the day-90 operation and eight positive muscle signals; Results has 21 rats at that operation and eight positives of 21; one figure has 8 of 16; the Discussion has 7 of 14; Table 4 lists seven plus-cases and ten minus-cases. Table 2's 10 versus 3 matches none of those splits. Results' own death cascade adds up (nine early deaths, 30−9=21, then six further deaths to 15 completers); the abstract's 16 does not. Tissues saved from two animals that died at revision can explain Table 4's 17 rows. They cannot explain eight versus seven positives.

Two lesser inconsistencies sit outside those tables. Vecuronium, used as functional proof of mixed transmission, is 0.04-0.05 mg/kg in the dosing table and 80 µg/kg (0.08 mg/kg) on the figure. Angiogenesis is said to average 2.57 in EMG-positive cases with individual scores of only 2 and 3, but Table 4 scores EMG-positive case 6 as 1; the EMG-negative average 1.3 does match that table.

The Combined Wei-Lachin interval is internally consistent with p<0.0001. Whether an interval that tight can come from n=10/3 given the wide component intervals is a question this toolkit cannot settle, and it is not treated as an accusation. The descriptive surgical and histological narrative is a different kind of evidence and is not what these checks speak to.

I have no confidence in the accuracy of the statistical tables as printed.

questions_for_authors.question: Table 3 prints Muscle Marlene p=0.4146 (N1/N2=16/5, MW=0.6250) and Muscle Catoi p=0.4936 (N1/N2=11/2, MW=0.8182), which are the same digits as Table 2 NNTXDIAM and NNTXAREA, and Table 3 Combined is MW=0.5611, 95% CI 0.5456-0.5766, N1/N2=10/3, p<0.0001 — identical to Table 2 Combined. Could you send the Mann-Whitney / Wei-Lachin output actually computed for the two muscle rows and for their combination?
questions_for_authors.why: Settles whether Table 3 is a copied forest-plot template and what the muscle tests were.

questions_for_authors.question: Table 2 NNTXMAX prints MW=0.8000, 95% CI 0.5362 to 1.0000, p=0.9017 at N1/N2=10/3. Could you send the test output that produced that p-value and interval, including the U (or equivalent) and whether the test was two-sided or directional?
questions_for_authors.why: The interval excludes 0.5 while p=0.9017 does not, and 0.9017 is not an achievable Mann-Whitney p for 10 versus 3.

questions_for_authors.question: The abstract has 16 rats at the day-90 operation and eight positive CMAPs; Results has 21 rats at that operation and eight positives of 21; Figure 4 has 8 of 16; the Discussion has 7 of 14; Table 4 lists seven (+) and ten (−) cases; Table 2 uses 10/3. Could you send the analysis n for stimulus yes versus no used in Tables 2 and 3, and which animals were counted as CMAP-positive?
questions_for_authors.why: The grouping for the only significant combined test is not a single printed number.

questions_for_authors.question: Table 1 lists Vecuronium 0.04-0.05 mg/kg IV and Figure 5 lists 80 µg/kg. Could you send the dose actually given to rats 19, 21, 28 and 29?
questions_for_authors.why: The functional proof of mixed transmission uses this dose, and the two printed values are different quantities.
